Researchers used mass spectrometry for metabolomic profiling of patient sera. Low levels may lead to a decreased capacity for antioxidant defense against cellular stress. Chenodeoxyglycocholic acid remained 3 times higher during the recovery phase. This specific bile acid shows that liver impact can last longer even after the initial fever passes. These findings suggest new therapeutic targets for managing severe dengue. Understanding the disease pathogenesis helps in finding better medical treatments for patients.

generated_summary: Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases must have their substrate receptor subunits tightly controlled. This control ensures the cell maintains a balanced variety of these ligase machines. Unbalanced levels of substrate receptors can lead to the sequestration of core components. This competition for parts disrupts normal cellular functions. Misregulation of substrate receptor components in SCF ligases is associated with cancer. Many other diseases are also linked to these protein-marking errors. F-box proteins are typically regulated by autocatalytic ubiquitylation and proteasome-mediated degradation. This process happens when the proteins are part of an intact SCF complex. Researchers identified a new degradation pathway for the yeast F-box protein Met30. This pathway acts when Met30 is dissociated from the Skp1 protein. The new Met30 degradation pathway requires Cdc53/Cul1 but is independent of Skp1. It uses only specific parts of the usual machine to function. This pathway is essential for chromosome stability and defense against heavy metal stress. It specifically helps yeast cells recover from stress caused by cadmium. The study assigns biological functions to a sub-complex of Cdc53, Rbx1, and Cdc34. This smaller team of proteins works independently of the Skp1 component.
